segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — January 22, 2019:

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award for Officer Diego Garcia

segments.text: Mayor Frost gave examples of Officer Diego Garcia's work in the community and thanked him and the Police Department for their service after Garcia received the NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award.
View minutes, page 2

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: Mr. Bunker thanked Officer Garcia, the Police Department, and the Fire Department for their service. He shared a story of officers acting exceptionally and saving lives.
View minutes, page 2

entities.speaker: Barbara Christiansen
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: Council Member Christiansen thanked the Police and Fire Departments for their service.
View minutes, page 2

Council Member Shelton reported that he had previewed technology intended to reduce emergency-dispatch response times and asked the Council to consider implementing it in the City. He also thanked Officer Garcia for his service.
View minutes, page 2

entities.speaker: Kevin J. Barnes
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: Council Member Barnes thanked Officer Garcia, the Police Department, and the Fire Department and stated that it took many people to make the City run efficiently.
View minutes, page 2
Council Member Taylor thanked the Police Department for its service.
View minutes, page 2

entities.speaker: Robert E. Shelton
entities.remark-context: Public-safety services contract with Cedar Hills

segments.text: Council Member Shelton raised concerns about contract language allowing Cedar Hills to leave the public-safety agreement and the financial effect that could have on American Fork. He stated that American Fork might not be able to afford the new station without Cedar Hills unless it imposed a significant property-tax increase and said the City needed to plan for that possibility.
View minutes, pages 3–4

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: Public-safety services contract with Cedar Hills

segments.text: Mayor Frost stated that American Fork needed a second station regardless of what happened with Cedar Hills. He said it would be beneficial for Cedar Hills to participate, but the city needed an opportunity to leave if it was unhappy, and he described the agreement as fair to both parties. He also said American Fork had a good working relationship with Cedar Hills.
View minutes, pages 3–4

entities.speaker: Kyle Maurer
entities.remark-context: Lease agreement for six police vehicles

segments.text: During consideration of a $245,098 lease agreement for six police vehicles, Mr. Maurer explained that the master lease would establish the termination terms and was structured like an auto loan.
View minutes, page 6

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Public-safety services contract with Cedar Hills

segments.text: Mr. Bunker explained that the agreement would renew automatically and discussed how the contract's term and annual increase would operate. He also stated that the police-services portion was structured as a two-year contract with a 3% increase at the end of two years and a 180-day termination clause.
View minutes, pages 3–4
